kicker: gpu-lexer, a highlighter with no grammars

scenes.headline: How a tiny model highlights code on the GPU
scenes.sub: gpu-lexer labels every part of a file at once, with no grammar.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Dovetail! Today: a highlighter with no grammar that colours a whole file at once.

scenes.text: Treat source code as a one-dimensional image. Split it into parts, then let a tiny model label every part in parallel.
scenes.say: Treat code as a one dimensional image, and label every part in parallel.

scenes.title: The usual lexer, and this one

left.title: A grammar per language
items: One state, carried character by character
Each step needs the one before
A new grammar for every language
left.say: A normal lexer walks one character at a time, with a grammar per language.

right.title: gpu-lexer
items: Context from a scan and a tree
right.say: gpu-lexer is never told the language, and labels every part at once.

steps.say: One CPU pass splits the source into words, spaces and symbols.
On the GPU, each part becomes thirty two learned channels.
A learned scan carries context in both directions.
A tree merges blocks into one file summary, then sends it back down.
Every part gets one of nine classes, and equal neighbours merge into spans.

parts.note: a gate between zero and one
parts.say: The gate a decides how much old state survives.
b is what the current part writes in.

parts.note: affine maps compose into affine maps
parts.say: Two of these maps in a row are still one map, so any stretch of code shrinks to two numbers per channel.

scenes.title: How the GPU runs the scan

items.say: Cut the parts into blocks of thirty two.

items.text: Fold each block to a pair
items.say: Fold every block into one pair, all at once.
A short scan tells each block where it starts.
Each block replays from its true start.

steps.say: Here is the tree from Shu Ding's animation.
Whole file context comes back down to every part.

scenes.title: Ten copies of three.min.js
scenes.note: Apple M4 Pro, median of three fresh workers
scenes.say: On five and a half million characters, gpu-lexer takes about two hundred and twenty milliseconds. Highlights takes about seventy five.

scenes.label: of the 3.8x came from the code, same runner before and after
scenes.say: And the three point eight times? Measured the same way before and after, the code is worth one point three seven.

scenes.text: A gated affine map composes into another one, so any stretch of code fits in two numbers per channel.
scenes.say: These maps compose into maps of the same size, so the scan never grows.
